ai.definition: Agentic RAG, or Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Self-Correction Loops, is an AI architecture where agents iteratively retrieve and evaluate contextual information to generate responses, incorporating self-correction mechanisms for improved accuracy.
ai.howItWorks: Agents repeatedly fetch relevant data from a knowledge base, assess the retrieved content for relevance and accuracy, and then use this context to refine their response. The process includes feedback loops that allow for continuous improvement of the generated output.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the limitations of traditional RAG systems by enhancing context-awareness and self-corrective capabilities, leading to more accurate and relevant responses in complex knowledge-based tasks.
ai.buildProcess: Developed through iterative refinement of AI models and algorithms, integrating advanced natural language processing techniques and feedback mechanisms. Requires substantial computational resources for training and testing.
ai.costDrivers: High computational requirements, data storage costs, and the need for large-scale datasets. Additionally, continuous model optimization and maintenance incur ongoing expenses.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to move from research labs into early commercial applications as more robust models are developed and validated in real-world scenarios.
ai.regulation: Currently not heavily regulated but may face scrutiny under data privacy laws and AI ethics guidelines. Regulatory frameworks will likely evolve as the technology matures.
ai.risks: Data bias, security vulnerabilities, potential misuse of generated content, and ethical concerns related to decision-making autonomy.
ai.profitability: Potential for high profitability in enterprise solutions where accurate knowledge extraction and synthesis are critical, but current market penetration is limited due to early stage development.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected advancements in model efficiency, broader integration with existing AI systems, and enhanced self-correction mechanisms. Potential for increased adoption in industries requiring sophisticated information processing.

glossary.def: AI entities that perform iterative retrieval and evaluation of context before generating responses.
The process of fetching relevant information from a knowledge base or database based on the input query.
The creation of new content, such as text or speech, based on the retrieved context and agent evaluation.
Feedback mechanisms that allow agents to refine their responses by incorporating corrections from previous iterations or external validation.
The relevant information or data points retrieved and used by the agents for generating accurate and contextually appropriate responses.

subsystems.name: Query planner
subsystems.role: turns a user question into a search plan: what to look up, how many queries, and in what order.
parts: routing rules (retrieve at all, or answer directly?)

subsystems.name: Retriever
subsystems.role: finds candidate passages from a corpus.
parts: keyword index (e.g. BM25) for exact terms

subsystems.name: Reranker and filter
subsystems.role: narrows many candidates to the few passages that actually answer the question.

subsystems.name: Generator
subsystems.role: reads the selected passages and writes an answer with citations.

subsystems.name: Critic / verifier
subsystems.role: checks whether each claim in the draft is supported by the retrieved text, and estimates confidence.

subsystems.name: Agent controller
subsystems.role: runs the loop, decides when to re-query, and stops.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the corpus
buildSteps.detail: Parse documents into passages of a few hundred tokens with overlap, keeping headings, dates and source IDs attached to each chunk.

buildSteps.title: Index it twice
buildSteps.detail: Compute a dense embedding for every chunk and store it in a vector index; at the same time build an inverted keyword index so rare names and numbers are not lost.

buildSteps.title: Wrap retrieval as a tool
buildSteps.detail: Expose search as a callable function the model can invoke with a query string, and return passages with metadata rather than raw text.

buildSteps.title: Write the agent loop
buildSteps.detail: Prompt the model to plan, call the tool, read results, judge sufficiency, and either answer or issue a reformulated query. This plan-act-observe pattern follows the ReAct approach published in 2022.

buildSteps.title: Add self-critique
buildSteps.detail: Before returning, have the model break its draft into atomic claims and mark each as supported, unsupported or contradicted by the retrieved passages — the style of self-reflective RAG work such as Self-RAG (2023).

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the stopping rule
buildSteps.detail: Set a maximum number of iterations and a confidence threshold; if the threshold is never met, return an explicit 'insufficient evidence' answer instead of guessing.

buildSteps.title: Build an evaluation set
buildSteps.detail: Collect a few hundred real questions with known correct passages and answers, then measure retrieval recall, answer faithfulness and whether citations actually contain the claims.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Add caching of repeated queries, latency and token budgets, per-request tracing, and an escalation path to a human when confidence is low.

prerequisites.tech: Dense text embeddings and vector search
prerequisites.why: semantic retrieval is the base layer; without it there is nothing for the agent to reason over.

prerequisites.tech: Instruction-tuned LLMs with long context and tool calling
prerequisites.why: the loop depends on a model that can emit structured calls and hold many passages at once.
cheap first-pass retrieval is noisy; a second scoring pass is what makes re-querying worthwhile.
models are poor at knowing when they are wrong, so the confidence threshold this design relies on is unreliable.
you cannot tune loop depth or thresholds without repeatable faithfulness and retrieval metrics.

prerequisites.tech: Latency and cost control for multi-step inference
prerequisites.why: several model calls per question multiply cost and delay, which limits use in interactive products.

pathway.milestone: single-pass RAG with a reranker is standard in enterprise search assistants
pathway.unlocks: grounded answers with citations over a private document set.

pathway.milestone: corrective loops that rewrite the query or fall back to web search when retrieval is weak, as in Corrective RAG (2024)
pathway.unlocks: robustness to messy or sparse internal corpora.

pathway.milestone: claim-level verification and abstention become routine
pathway.unlocks: auditable answers in regulated settings such as medicine, law and finance.

pathway.milestone: learned controllers that decide retrieval depth from measured answer quality rather than fixed thresholds
pathway.unlocks: predictable latency and cost alongside reliable factuality.
